judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: Lead photo of the article: an aerial view of a Petrobras FPSO platform ship at sea (crop and screenshot). Its alt is the editorial caption, also shown visibly below the image: "Petrobras: dados de produção do 3º tri bateram recorde (MAURO PIMENTEL/AFP/Getty Images)". claimTrue: record production data is not something the photo shows, so the sentence holds of the capture. elementFails: skeptic reading is no: the photo is a generic illustration whose purpose is to set the topic, and the alt identifies its subject (Petrobras, its oil production); no documented failure applies (it is not a filename or placeholder, F30). But it says nothing of what is depicted and duplicates the caption, and a strict auditor would fail it for not serving an equivalent purpose, so competent auditors would reasonably disagree. captureDiffers: the live HTML and the styled screenshot match the snapshot. Label uncertain.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Newsletter sign-up field ("Saiba investir melhor"), <input id=email type=email name=email> labelled "Seu e-mail", with no autocomplete attribute. It collects the user's own email address, an Input Purpose listed in WCAG 2.1 section 7; type=email gives the format, not whose address it is, and the only sufficient technique (H98) is missing. claimTrue: the snapshot shows no autocomplete and Chromium's form issue FormInputAssignedAutocompleteValueToIdOrNameAttributeError on this input, so both parts hold. captureDiffers: the live HTML has the identical input with no autocomplete. I looked for a reason it could pass (not user data, purpose set another way) and found none: true_positive.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Image link in a related-articles card: <a> > <figure> > span > img with alt ("Imagem referente à matéria: Arquivar ou trancar fotos no Google Fotos? Entenda a diferença"), no text, no aria-label, aria-labelledby or title; the headline is a separate adjacent link to the same href. claimTrue: the snapshot's CDP tree gives this link the name "" (Rampa's own 'name' field is raw <noscript> markup, a collector quirk, but the finding rests on the browser name). In the same tree every link that wraps its image in a <figure> has an empty name while hamburger-menu links with span-wrapped images include the alt, so Chrome does not carry the alt through the figure. elementFails: in Chrome/Edge, as users receive it at desktop width (hidden md:* shows it), the focusable link exposes no accessible name; the accname spec would recurse into the figure, but WCAG judges what accessibility-supported user agents expose, and axe-style link-name checks skip figure content too. Redundancy with the headline link does not give this link a name. captureDiffers: the live HTML (curl, fetched 2026-11-21) has the same figure/img/noscript structure and no naming attribute. The claim names the real defect (empty link name), so true_positive.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The "Invest" link at the start of the section sub-navigation (BTG Insights, Mercados, ...), href https://exame.com/invest/, the Exame Invest section page. claimTrue: the snapshot (and live HTML) has four links named Invest, three to /invest/ and one footer newsletter link to /newsletters/, and this one has no heading, list item or description around it, so the sentence holds. elementFails: no. Its own text states its purpose, going to the Invest section, which is where it leads; 2.4.4 asks whether each link's purpose can be determined, not that all links sharing a text share a destination (that is closer to 2.4.9 or a consistency rule). The ambiguous link, if any, is the footer one, not this. captureDiffers: the live page and the styled screenshot match. false_positive, criterion_misapplied.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: Thumbnail image that is the only content of a link to the article "Anthropic fecha em alta de 17%, longe da máxima, em estreia na bolsa". Its alt is that headline, which states the link's destination, the function a text alternative for an image link must convey (H30); the crop shows an Anthropic/Claude logo illustration, so nothing informative is lost for the link's purpose. The repetition of the adjacent headline link is a redundancy issue, not a 1.1.1 failure, and the img node itself exposes the alt (the empty name of the enclosing link is a 4.1.2 matter, reported separately). captureDiffers: the live HTML has the same img and alt. elementFails no, so Rampa's silence is correct: false_positive.
